correctness.rationale: With the stated signed-permutation convention the reflection lengths, interval ranks and relation K^2(w)=c^-1 w c agree. The rank reversal still takes chains to simplices. In the barycentric subdivision the dimensions of the faces in a flag are distinct, so a group element carrying a flag to itself fixes it pointwise. Taking flag orbits with their incidences therefore gives the ordinary geometric quotient, not an orbit poset or a Borel construction. The independent reconstruction gives 68/288/256 original simplices, 612/2112/1536 barycentric simplices and 77/264/192 quotient cells, with one orbit of four vertices and all other barycentric cell orbits of size eight. Contracting a tree leaves 188 loops and 192 triangular attaching words, with the last edge reversed. A relator that uses a generator just once can be made that generator by a free-basis change on the graph: cyclically write it as g^{±1}w with w in the other letters, then invert g if needed and replace it by gw. The pair consisting of this new loop and its filling disk can be contracted, updating all other words by the corresponding substitution; this is a homotopy equivalence of complexes, not just of presented groups. The independent replay performs 187 cancellations and leaves signed degrees (0,4,0,4,4) on one circle. Precomposing the five attaching loops with elementary Nielsen equivalences of their wedge subtracts one degree-four column from each redundant degree-four column, preserving the homotopy cofiber; the remaining degrees are (4,0,0,0,0). Integral boundaries compose to zero and have nonzero Smith factors 1^76 and (1^187,4), respectively. Since the map coker(d2) to im(d1) has free target and kernel H1, this also gives the asserted H1 torsion. H2 is free of rank four. This is a correct calculation for this one ordinary orbit space.

evidence: Reiner's type-B lattice is EL-shellable. Its proper rank-four order complex is pure of dimension two and hence a wedge of 2-spheres, in particular simply connected.

Armstrong's orbit-space theorem gives pi1(X/L)=L/N_L for a finite simplicial action on simply connected X, with N_L generated by point-fixing elements. In 1982, Theorem 4 applies: Proposition 3(a) supplies path lifting, and the remaining hypotheses are immediate for finite groups on this finite simplicial realization.

Dyer–Sieradski's 1973 theorem, part (1), classifies every connected finite 2-dimensional CW-complex with finite cyclic fundamental group by that cyclic group and rank H2; part (2) and the corollary also address simple homotopy type.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The general theorem applies to the actual orbit CW complex, not just to coverings or wedges known in advance. Once the finite cyclic fundamental group and Euler characteristic are recovered from the old subgroup data, a new explicit cancellation computation is not needed to infer the homotopy type.

evidence: Put G=<K>=C8 and H=<K^2>=C4. Since X is simply connected, Armstrong gives pi1(X/H)=H/N_H, a cyclic group, so it already equals its own abelianization. The older H1=Z/2 therefore forces N_H=<K^4>.

If an odd power of K fixed a point of X, that power generates G and hence its powers would make K^2 fix that point, contrary to K^2 not in N_H. Consequently N_G=N_H and Armstrong gives pi1(X/G)=G/<K^4>=Z/4.

The residual involution of G/H on X/H is free: if an H-orbit were fixed, some element in G minus H would fix a representative. Thus X/H -> X/G is a double cover of finite CW spaces and chi(X/G)=chi(X/H)/2=10/2=5.

Since the quotient is connected and 2-dimensional with finite H1, rank H2=chi-1=4 and H2 is free. Dyer–Sieradski now give P_4 wedge four 2-spheres, exactly the full statement, including the integral homology consequences.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: This is a direct implication of the earlier subgroup quotient theorem and classical classification, without any new case-specific calculation. The frozen claim that the prior subgroup homology does not imply this full homotopy type overlooks the fixed-point obstruction and the general cyclic classification.

evidence: Bessis–Reiner Section 6 after Conjecture 6.5 uses cw^-1, the inverse of the displayed K, with the same generated group. Its square is conjugation by c; K squared is its inverse conjugation, yielding the same subgroup H.
Dyer–Sieradski call S^1 with one degree-n 2-cell the pseudo-projective plane P_n. Their wedge with four spheres for n=4 is precisely the claimed Moore wedge.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Using the inverse generator does not change the ordinary quotient. Neither 'pseudo-projective plane' versus 'Moore space' nor rotation versus inverse rotation changes the implication; the subgroup and full-group quotients are distinct but connected by a double quotient.
